description: This false-colour satellite image depicts a landscape in North Western Spain, highlighting areas affected by recent fires. Large sections of the image appear dark blue and black, which, according to the surrounding context for "Burnt areas (except burnt forest)", indicates recently fire-affected land that is still mainly black. These burnt areas are interspersed with patches of bright red and magenta, representing healthy vegetation with high chlorophyll content, likely unaffected scrubland or forest. Lighter grey and brown areas are also visible, suggesting bare ground or agricultural fields. White lines delineate various parcels or land features across the landscape. The image serves as an example of burnt scrubland. The data source is credited to Eurostat, LUCAS (Land Use and Cover Area frame Survey).
